FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Sewing Machines Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. This standard was originally published in 1%7. This first revision has been undertaken to incorporate material details, rationalize the sixes due to revision of IS 1610 and make the standard more user and manufacturer friendly. Additional details about surface roughness have also been incorporated. For general requirements of sewing machine IS 1610 : 1989 `Household sewing machines - General requirement (second revr&n)' may be referred. A list of Indian Standards on sewing machines and the components is also given in Annex B. In the preparation of the original version of this standard, assistance had been derived from JIS B 9026 : 1%3 Oscillating shaft of sewing machine for home use, issued by Japanese Standards Association. The Japanese standard has remained unchanged after publication in 1%3. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (reltised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

HOUSEHOLD SEWING MACHINES OSCILLATING SHAFTS - SPECIFICATION
( First Revision )
1 SCOPE This Indian Standard (Firsr Revision) specifies the requirements for two types of oscillating shafts for sewing machines for household purposes. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below:
IS No.

3 TYPES The oscillating shaft shall be either Type A or Type B (see Fig. in Table 1 and Table 2) 4 MATERIAL The oscillating shafts shall be manufactured from a suitable carbon steel, such as 1503 of IS 4432 : 1988. 5 KARDNESS The bearing surfaces shall be heat treated to achieve a hardness value between 400 and 450 HV. 6 DIMENSIONS The main dimensions for oscillating shafts shall be as given in Table 1 and Table 2. 7 TOLERANCES 7.1 The radial run-out of oscillating shaft centre at points 35 mm from ends shall not exceed 0.01 mm. 7.2 The error in straightness shafts shall be within 0.08 mm of the oscillating

7.3 The error in ovality of the bearing diameters of the oscillating shafts shall be within 0.005 mm. 7.4 Tolerances on untoleranced dimensions shall conform to fine grade of IS 2102 (Part 1) : 1993.

8 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 8.1 The oscillating shafts shall be well finished and shall be free from defects, such as cracks, flaw, burrs and rust. 8.2 The bearing portion of the oscillating shaft shall be precision ground to a minimum surface finish value of Ra 0.4 pm. 9 DESIGNATION The oscillating shafts shall be designated by the part name, that is `Oscillating Shaft'; Type and number of this Indian Standard. An oscillating shaft of Type B shall be designated as: Oscillating Shaft B IS 4188 10 SAMPLING Unless otherwise agreed upon between the supplier and the purchaser, the sampling plan as given in Annex A shall be followed. For further information reference may be made to IS 2500 (Part 1) : 1992. 11 MARKING 11.1 Each piece of the oscillating shaft shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the following:

a)
b)

Source of manufacture and trade-mark, if any; and Type of oscillating shah.

11.2 BIS Certification Marking The product may also be marked with the Standard Mark 11.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provision of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made there under. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 12 PACKING Each oscillating shaft shall be given a suitable antirust coating and wrapped in polythene paper or bags. The wrapped oscillating shaft shall be securely packed in accordance with the best prevalent trade practice. Each package shall bear the following: a) b) c) Name of the manufacturer if any lype; and Designation. and trade mark;

ANNEX A
(Clause 10)
SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY A-l SCALE OF SAMPLING A-l.1 Lot In any consignment, all the oscillating shafts of the same type and manufactured from the same material under essentially similar conditions of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. A-l.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the specification, tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. The number of oscillating shafts to be selected at random for this purpose shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 3. A-l.3 If the oscillating shafts are packed individually, IS 4905 : 1968 shall be used in order to ensure the randomness of selection. A-l.4 If the oscillating shafts are packed in different cartons, a suitable number of cartons (not less than 20 percent of the total in the lot subject to a minimum of 2) shall be chosen at random. From each of the cartons so chosen, an approximately equal number of oscillating shafts shall be picked up from its different parts so as to obtain the required number of oscillating shafts specified in co1 2 of Table 3. A-2 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY A-2.1 The oscillating shafts selected according to A-l.2 and A-l.3 or A-l.4 shall be examined for dimensions (see 6), tolerances (see 7) and workmanship and finish (see 8). If the number of oscillating shafts failing to meet one or more of the requirements mentioned above is less than or equal to the permissible number of defectives given in co1 3 of Table 3, the lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of these characteristics. A-2.2 In case of those lots which have been found satisfactory according to A-2.1, a number of oscillating shafts equal to the sample size indicated in co1 4 of Table 3, shall be subjected to hardness test (see 5). Any oscillating shaft failing to meet the requirement for hardness shall be considered to be defective. A-2.2.1 If no defectives are found among the oscillating shafts subjected to the` hardness test (see A-2.2), the lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of the specification, otherwise not.

llureau of Indian Standards

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bctreau ofhndian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'. This lndian Standard has been developed from Dot : No. LM 18 ( 0043 ).
